newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil on verge of setting CVRD base price.
newsitem.headline: Brazil on verge of setting CVRD base price.

text.p: Brazil is on the verge of setting the base price for mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), Latin America's biggest privatization to date and expected to attract a swarm of foreign investors.

Officials said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir was due to approve the final details of CVRD's bid specifications later Tuesday and submit them to the National Privatization Council (CND) Wednesday morning.
"Everything indicates that tomorrow we will finally have put this stage (of setting the price) behind us," said a spokeswoman for Kandir.
The CVRD sell-off has been delayed before and officials declined to guarantee definitively that the base price and firm auction date would be made public after the CND meeting.

Even Kandir himself, talking to reporters in Sao Paulo Monday, was a touch cagey. "There's always a risk (of a delay) but I think it unlikely," he was quoted by the financial daily Gazeta Mercantil as saying.

At National Development Bank (BNDES) headquarters in Rio de Janeiro, officials testily declined to confirm the document was being given the final touches before being sent to Brasilia. "We can't say anything and won't. This is a really sensitive subject," said a spokesman.

The sell-off of CVRD, the world's largest iron ore exporter and a major producer of gold, copper and other metals, has raised national passions in Brazil and is seen as a water test of the government's commitment to privatization.

Last week the government decided that half of the proceeds from the sale of its 51 percent stake would go to an Economic Reconstruction Fund and be used for infrastructure projects. Furthermore, CVRD and BNDES will sign risk contracts to jointly explore and develop undiscovered deposits, ensuring Brazil does not miss out on any possible future discoveries. Congress watchers say the moves were certain to douse the
fiery opposition of some politicians, concerned CVRD's future private sector owners would not continue to finance regional development as the firm has always done.

The sale itself is expected to kick off in April when a controlling stake of 40-45 percent of voting shares is put under the hammer. The initial block sale will be followed by offerings to staff and then on domestic and foreign exchanges.
To assure nationalists the government is not selling off total control over strategic resources, the National Treasury will hold a perpetual "golden share", or right of veto.

CVRD is valued in the market at between $10-12 billion, making Brasilia's potential receipts some $5.0-6.0 billion. The group made a net profit of 280 million reais in January to September 1996 on gross revenue of 2.171 billion reais against a net of 209 million reais on revenue of 2.159 billion reais in the same period a year before.
Of major international mining resources companies, analysts say Japanese investors are expected to lead the pack into the auction, with Nippon Steel Corp reportedly heading a consortium.
Australia's WMC Ltd and South Africa's Gencor Ltd and Anglo American have also expressed interest.

The CND was scheduled to start meeting at 1000 local Wednesday (1300 GMT). Officials said it was likely to be short and Kandir might brief journalists an hour later. (-- Brasilia newsroom 55-61-2230358))
